short_description: Non-enveloped, wheel-shaped triple-layered icosahedral dsRNA virus (~75 nm across the smooth rim, ~100 nm including its spikes) of the Sedoreoviridae (genus Rotavirus); named from Latin rota, "wheel", because in negative-stain EM the short blunt VP4 spikes around a sharp rim make it look like a spoked wheel, it packs 11 double-stranded RNA segments inside a VP2 core wrapped in VP6 and an outer VP7 shell, and it is the leading cause of severe dehydrating gastroenteritis in infants worldwide.

colour_legend.vp7_outer: cool cerulean / sky-blue glassy outer shell (T=13 trimer mosaic)
colour_legend.vp4_spikes: warm amber-gold, short blunt bilobed spikes (VP8* head paler ochre, VP5* body deeper amber)
colour_legend.vp6_intermediate: muted sea-green / teal pillars (the group antigen layer)
colour_legend.dsrna_segments: coppery orange double-stranded rods, eleven of them, coiled as a spooled bundle
colour_legend.vp1_rdrp: deep indigo lobe at a five-fold vertex (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase)
colour_legend.vp3_capping: warm terracotta-brick lobe beside VP1 (capping enzyme)
colour_legend.channels: shadowed slate-grey openings sunk through the VP7 and VP6 layers
colour_legend.background: neutral dark charcoal (aged cream paper for the watercolour plate)
colour_legend.note: A virion has no pigment of its own; every colour here is teaching convention (see reference/colors.md). Electron micrographs are greyscale — the blue of the CDC PHIL reference plate is digital false colour added afterwards. Keep this structure→colour map identical across textbook, SEM, 3d and watercolour.

do_not_draw: lipid envelope or membrane bilayer of any kind (rotavirus is NON-enveloped — the single most serious error)
long club-shaped or mushroom-headed coronavirus spikes, a corona of clubs, HA/NA-style projections or a fuzzy fringe (the VP4 spikes are SHORT and blunt)
a helical, rod-shaped, filamentous or bullet-shaped capsid
a single smooth featureless sphere with no layers, no rim and no spikes
single-stranded RNA, DNA or a B-form double helix with drawn base-pair rungs
one single unsegmented genome molecule — there must be ELEVEN separate dsRNA segments
a bacteriophage tail, base plate, collar or legs; turret-like spikes at the vertices (rotavirus has no turrets)
a nucleus, ribosomes, mitochondria, cytoplasm or any cell organelle
a face, eyes, limbs or any anthropomorphism (outside the separate kids' coloring page)
any text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks baked into the image

reference.note: Verified 2026-08-20 with curl: HTTP 200, content-type image/tiff, 10,846,694 bytes; native pixel size 2700 x 2083 px, RGB, decoded cleanly by Pillow (real baseline TIFF, not an upscale). This is the iconic rotavirus plate: a dense field of intact triple-layered particles, each showing the sharp outer rim with short radiating spikes over a lighter hub — the 'spoked wheel' that gave the genus its name — with several well-isolated particles near the frame edges suitable for a single-particle crop. Colour is digital false colour applied by CDC; the unmanipulated greyscale original of exactly the same frame is PHIL #273 (first alternative below). A 700 x 540 px JPEG of the same image exists at https://wwwn.cdc.gov/phil/PHIL_Images/178/178_lores.jpg — do not use it as if it were the full-resolution file.
